checks: Checked original note 7b76d58a056349ae, §§1–3, (1)–(7), including the fixed-roof scope and the finite triangle comparison. The affine second-order claim in §4 is outside the frozen statement.

The chord has the asserted sign relative to the concave roof inside and outside I. The endpoint comparison makes the chord nonnegative on [0,1]. Its mean over the centered interval equals its global mean, so the deficit is (2A+B)/3 and the L1 norm is A+B. By nonnegativity and continuity, zero deficit is exactly the affine case.

The strip over the base triangle has added area epsilon Z, with Z>0. Its normalized area measure converges weakly to psi(s)/Z on r=0, by uniform continuity. Of the three barycentrics (-r,s,1-s+r), the first is zero on the facet; the other two meet level 1/3 only at singletons of zero limiting mass.

On r=0 the canonical upper-cap count is 1+1_I away from the two endpoints. For d=2, t=epsilon Z, the normalized derivative from the accepted theorem is ((Z+int_I psi)/3-(4/9)Z)/V=E/(3V). This theorem concerns the maximizing depth over all ordinary closed cuts and applies beyond the old centroid.

For 1-epsilon b>0, the right vertex is at s_*=(1+epsilon a)/(1-epsilon b), and s_*-1=epsilon ell(1)/(1-epsilon b) is nonnegative. The possible exterior corner has base length s_*-1 and height epsilon ell(1), giving J_epsilon; if ell(1)=0 this corner is empty up to a null boundary. The two other area differences follow by vertical integration of the signed roof difference.

The normalized density overlap is intersection area divided by the larger area. Subtracting this from one gives the displayed maximum of the two exclusive areas divided by the larger area. The quotient by epsilon tends to max(A,B)/V because J_epsilon is second order. Cap discrepancy is no greater than TV and the infimum is no greater than the discrepancy to the displayed admissible triangle.

When E>0, max(A,B)>0 and max(A,B)≤3E, so c<1/9 makes the limiting excess strictly larger than c times the limiting TV quotient. This gives the small-epsilon comparison without attainment of the triangle infimum. For the affine case the conclusion only requires the first-order coefficient and TV quotient to vanish.

Checked exact arithmetic independently on the unit tent psi(s)=min(2s,2-2s): Z=1/2, the central integral is 5/18, A=1/18, B=2/9 and the depth coefficient is 2/27. For psi(s)=s and epsilon=1/4, A=B=0 and the exterior triangle has area 1/24, agreeing with J_epsilon.

Provides a depth-to-cap-discrepancy bound for an inner body of an enclosing simplex with all facet-centroid contacts and a small relative inner radius loss. The roof family is an outward perturbation of the reference triangle; the explicit secant triangle can fail to contain the roof body. The exact first-order coefficient and comparison cost are new here.
